assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin biology moved from the discovery of proglucagon-derived GLP-1 actions on islets, gut and brain to long-acting receptor agonists that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Few recent discoveries combine mechanistic originality, a clean physiological chain and population-scale medical impact; the neuroendocrine appetite and reward angle is also of interest from a neuropharmacology viewpoint.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, receptor pharmacology), Holst (GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic physiology) and Knudsen (design of the acylated analogues that became liraglutide and semaglutide) form a defensible three-person split of physiology, mechanism and translation. Mojsov's early peptide work is a real credit question, and my recollection is that other pioneers not on this list, such as Habener, also contributed; I cannot verify the precise priority claims.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is confirmed by many large independent trials and real-world use across multiple agents; the biology is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between peptide discovery (Mojsov and others) and drug development is contested.
Knudsen's contribution is industrial, and the committee would have to be comfortable honouring translational drug design alongside physiology.
Long-term safety and CNS mechanisms of weight loss are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib was the proof of principle for rationally targeted kinase inhibition in cancer, turning chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition. The concept (oncogenic kinase as druggable driver) is original, clear and has reshaped oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the chemistry and biology that identified the compound, Druker drove the clinical translation and trials, and Sawyers contributed key resistance biology and second-generation inhibitors; this trio is a natural configuration. The upstream discovery of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore, Groffen and others) lies outside the list and is a source of credit-boundary questions.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data and many independent confirmations; the paradigm has been extended to other kinase-driven cancers. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Boundary with the earlier discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion.
Whether Sawyers's resistance work or others' roles better complete the trio is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new therapeutic modality, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and now spreading to autoimmune disease. The idea of redirecting T cells with synthetic receptors and costimulation is original and its impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulated CARs, preclinical proof), June (clinical translation in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy foundations and early CAR trials) are a plausible set, though Eshhar, Gross, Kalos, Brentjens, Maus and others have strong claims and the true core is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of clinical follow-up confirm benefit in hematologic cancers; solid tumours remain unresolved, and toxicity and secondary malignancy issues are being managed.
uncertainties: Crowded credit field; a three-person limit may leave out Eshhar and other founders.
Efficacy limited largely to hematologic malignancies so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is among the most widely used experimental tools in neuroscience, including circuit studies in Parkinson's disease, depression and addiction models. Originality and breadth of impact are very high, though its direct medical impact is still emerging, mainly in retinal restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated millisecond-scale neuronal control; Miesenböck's earlier photo-activation work is also relevant. A three-person split necessarily omits several defensible names, and this is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed across thousands of laboratories; long since stable, and recognition is timely to somewhat late.
uncertainties: Credit among six listed names is hard to restrict to three.
Therapeutic translation is limited relative to the tool's scientific influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that BCL-2 acts by blocking cell death rather than driving proliferation defined a new class of oncogene and the core apoptotic regulatory axis, directly enabling venetoclax for CLL and other BH3-mimetics. Mechanistic clarity and clinical consequence are both strong.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the Walter and Eliza Hall work on Bcl-2 and the Myc/Bcl-2 cooperation; Vaux demonstrated survival function in the 1988 work and Strasser extended it to the pathway. Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Cleary also have claims for the translocation and mechanism; I cannot independently verify the full priority record.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by decades of work; targeted therapy is approved and used, so the discovery and its application are both mature. Apoptosis itself was recognized in 2002, which could weigh against a perceived overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize on programmed cell death.
Credit competition with Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Cleary, who are not on this list's credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infant motor neuron disease into a treatable one. It is an elegant mechanism-to-therapy story that validates splice-switching oligonucleotides.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the target sequence, and Bennett led the oligonucleotide chemistry and development at Ionis; the pair is a compact configuration. Contributions of others (for example Hua, Singh and Biogen clinical teams) are not on the credited list and may complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong randomized trial and long-term outcome data; the principle has been extended, so recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Many consider the origin of SMN2-directed antisense a team effort.
Whether it reads as a drug approval rather than a fundamental discovery for the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are among the great preventive-medicine successes, with population data showing sharp declines in cervical precancer and cancer. The VLP concept is original and the impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (NCI) made the L1 VLP immunogen work, and Frazer (with Zhou) contributed early VLP production; Zhou's death in 1999 and the related industrial parallel work are credit complications. The HPV-cancer link was already recognized in 2008.
assessment.maturity: Mature; real-world effectiveness is well documented over more than fifteen years across many countries.
uncertainties: Zhou Jian is not creditable and priority is contested among several groups.
Partial overlap with the 2008 prize for HPV discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that blocking it ameliorates rheumatoid arthritis established cytokine blockade as a therapeutic class, now used across many inflammatory diseases. Impact is vast and the translational logic is clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini form a natural pair for the anti-TNF concept and the clinical proof; other contributors in the TNF biology and antibody engineering story (Cerami, Vilcek and others) are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; decades of clinical data and several biologics, with biosimilars now widespread. Recognition is arguably late.
uncertainties: Fundamental discovery of TNF versus its therapeutic application may split credit.
Recent prizes in immune tolerance may influence timing.
